title: Toxicology waiting, pending certificates, and paperwork limbo after overdose death

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0021 suicide/overdose postvention high-gate layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no method detail, no crisis/therapy/legal/forensic advice.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, and seed-cue factoring during rev0021
limitations: Public sources support vocabulary, safe-rendering constraints, postvention framing, stigma boundaries, and review routing only.
No method/means detail, scene detail, note content, private family narrative, toxicology speculation, or case-identifying fact is admissible from this record.

Records must not advise readers how to respond to a suicide or overdose event, investigate a death, disclose a death, write an obituary, handle belongings, or manage a child/school/community response.

moment.plain_scene: Families may wait for toxicology, amended certificates, or official wording while grief is already underway.
ordinary_language_queries: waiting for cause of death overdose

content_layers.observation_text: Families may wait for toxicology, amended certificates, or official wording while grief is already underway.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The sources support treating this as a postvention/safe-language/stigma-boundary record, while keeping details, support needs, disclosure decisions, school/work/community responses, cause/manner words, and survivor risk dependent on qualified local support, policy, culture, and specialist review.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: For DeathVocab, this is an afterdeath language and harm-boundary record. The archive can make the social and linguistic room legible without publishing what would endanger, identify, blame, instruct, or sensationalize.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Render only as safe-language and boundary grammar after suicide-prevention/postvention, overdose-stigma, privacy, pediatric if applicable, official-trace if applicable, and publication review. Do not render method, location, note, toxicology detail, scene detail, crisis advice, or family script.

what_this_is_not: a legal, forensic, clinical, school, workplace, or media instruction manual
a public scene, note, toxicology, photo, or case-detail surface
uncertainties: Local law, official process, school/work/community policy, cultural practice, survivor needs, and family privacy may change how this vocabulary can be used.
Public sources do not replace consented testimony from survivors, responders, clinicians, or community postvention workers.
Cause, manner, intent, substance involvement, and support needs must not be inferred from a public-facing record.
content_layers.lay_orientation: This record exists because some deaths leave people not only grieving, but also navigating stigma, unsafe language, official words, privacy hazards, and support needs. The archive can name the pattern without making your situation public or giving instructions.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future work must route this record through suicide-safe messaging, overdose-stigma, postvention, privacy, official-trace if applicable, pediatric if applicable, clinical/mental-health, and publication-language review before any public rendering.
language_notes: Avoid method, means, location, note contents, graphic imagery, single-cause explanations, blame, spectacle, and fatalism.
For overdose, avoid reducing the person to substance use, criminality, or toxicology.
Include resource-routing posture if any public surface is ever attempted, but do not turn the archive into crisis care.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0021 from public-source synthesis and seed-cue factoring; no private account, no survivor quote, no official validation, no clinical or legal validation, no public release.

evidence_class.limitations: No private testimony, no scene detail, no method detail, no crisis intervention, no therapy, no legal or forensic advice.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not include names, dates, rare locations, note contents, method/means details, photos, screenshots, direct messages, toxicology specifics, police/EMS narrative, unusual circumstances, school/workplace identifiers, or family facts that could identify a person or living survivor.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record for crisis care, mental-health triage, overdose response, substance-use treatment, diagnosis, prognosis, or clinical decision-making.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer reporting duties, school or workplace duties, official process, family rights, cause/manner status, property handling, child communication, or public-disclosure obligations from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not universalize what families, traditions, clergy, schools, workplaces, or communities should say or do after suicide or overdose loss.
safety.method_silence: Absolute: no method/means specifics, no location specificity that implies method, no note contents, no image/screenshot/scene detail, no response steps, no toxicology spectacle.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical, mental-health, crisis, overdose-response, legal, forensic, school, workplace, media, funeral, or family-disclosure advice; qualified local support and authorities govern actual cases.
safety_notes: Postvention records are high risk for contagion, identification, stigma, blame, and survivor harm.
Method-silence is a design property of the cube, not an optional tone preference.
Do not treat one source, one official word, one family story, or one public memorial as the whole truth of the death.
